info.title: IdentyClaw Federated Peer API (RODiT)
info.description:
# IdentyClaw federated peer API

Reusable pattern for **federated API authentication**: IdentyClaw **Passport** holders prove possession of their keys against **this peer**, receive a **peer-minted JWT**, and call protected routes. Built on `@rodit/rodit-auth-be` 9.x.

CRUDA (`/api/cruda/*`) is only a sample protected resource — replace it with your domain.

## Federation model

| Identity surface | Role |
| --- | --- |
| **IdentyClaw home** (`https://api.identyclaw.com`) | Passport / HOLA enrollment. Home JWT does **not** authorize this peer's protected routes. |
| **This peer** (your `apiEndpoint`) | Own RODiT service credentials. Mint JWTs via `POST /api/login`. Clients must login **against this base URL**. |

Each federated peer is an independent auth boundary. Agents and apps remint a JWT per `apiEndpoint`. Do not reuse a token from another peer or from home.

```
Passport keys (Ed25519)
        │
        ▼
GET /api/login/timestamp  →  challenge (timestamp + timestamp_iso)
        │
        ▼
Sign UTF-8: identifier + timestamp_iso  →  POST /api/login
        │
        ▼
Peer JWT (Authorization: Bearer)  →  protected routes + METHOD_PERMISSION_MAP
```

## Authentication (raw)

1. `GET /api/login/timestamp` — challenge pair from this peer.
2. Sign UTF-8 `identifier + timestamp_iso` (Ed25519 → base64url). Identifier is Passport `roditid` (12 letters) or NEAR `accountid` (64-hex).
3. `POST /api/login` — send signature + exactly one of `timestamp` / `timestamp_iso`.
4. Call protected routes with `Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token>` (body field is `jwt_token`, not `token`).
5. `POST /api/logout` — invalidate session (`authenticateForLogout` allows expired JWTs with valid signature).

## OpenClaw / agents

Preferred: `identyclaw_ensure_session({ apiEndpoint })` then `identyclaw_request({ method, path, apiEndpoint })`. The plugin caches the peer JWT and never returns it to the model.

Discovery: `GET /`, `GET /.well-known/mcp`, `GET /api/mcp/resource/doc:skills`.

## Authorization

Protected showcase routes under `/api/cruda/*` require both:

1. Valid peer JWT (`authenticate`)
2. Verb allowed by `METHOD_PERMISSION_MAP` (`authorize`) — keys such as `create`, `list`, `read`, `update`, `destroy`

Sessions admin follows the same RODiT permission patterns. See config `METHOD_PERMISSION_MAP`.

## Errors

`{ error: { code, message, details? }, requestId, timestamp }` — see `components.schemas.ErrorResponse`.

## Scaffold usage

1. Keep auth, discovery, health, swagger, and permission-map wiring.
2. Replace or extend `/api/cruda` with your resources; mount with authenticate + authorize.
3. Point `SERVICE_NAME` / nginx / OpenAPI `servers` at your peer hostname.
4. Publish this OpenAPI as the contract for Passport holders integrating with your peer.

Returns a simple homepage message

post.description: MCP Streamable HTTP transport. Send `initialize` first; subsequent calls need `Mcp-Session-Id`. Tools: `list_resources`, `get_resource`. JWT is optional. Do not use this as a REST GET for docs — use `/.well-known/mcp` or `/api/mcp/*`.

400.description: MCP session required or invalid initialize

get.description: SSE stream for an existing MCP session. Requires `Mcp-Session-Id` from initialize. Bare GET without a session returns 400 `MCP_TRANSPORT_SESSION_REQUIRED`.

delete.description: Closes the MCP Streamable HTTP session identified by `Mcp-Session-Id`.

get.description: Federated login step 1. Returns synchronized Unix seconds (`timestamp`) and canonical ISO-8601 (`timestamp_iso`) for the Ed25519 signing payload. Fetch a fresh pair from **this** peer immediately before each login; do not reuse challenges across peers or attempts.

post.description: Federated login step 2. Ed25519 challenge-response against **this** peer. Signed payload is UTF-8 `identifier + timestamp_iso` (no separator). Identifier is Passport `roditid` or NEAR `accountid`. Provide exactly one of `timestamp` or `timestamp_iso` from the same GET /api/login/timestamp response. Returns `jwt_token` for Bearer use on this peer only.

New-Token.description: Same JWT as jwt_token in body

post.description: Invalidates the peer session for this apiEndpoint. Uses authenticateForLogout so expired JWTs may still be accepted when the signature is valid. Does not invalidate IdentyClaw home or other peers' sessions.

requestBody.description: JSON body required (may be empty). Content-Type must be application/json.

415.description: Content-Type must be application/json when body is sent

get.description: Debug helper: returns the authenticated user object from the peer JWT. Use after login to verify federation against this apiEndpoint.

200.description: Current user claims from JWT token

user.description: Authenticated user object from this peer JWT (`req.user`)
